verdict_reason: The code computes the estimand the repo defines -- the mean per-token cosine to the ROW-CENTRED output-projection row of the target token minus a within-document frequency-matched minimum-collision control -- and I found no value-changing counterexample on that domain. Analytic anchor: on the centred simplex whose exact margin is 4/3, the task returns 1.3333332538604736 (rel 5.96e-08, float32 eps) BIT-IDENTICALLY at every scale from 1e-30 to 1e30 and under independent rescaling of h and W (h*1e-20/W*1e20, h*3e-23/W*1, h*1e20/W*1e-20 all return the same bits); all four normalisation sites now go through safe_unit_rows_torch (consistency.py:143,144,233,260) with zero F.normalize calls left, so round-3 codex's RED (0.0099999990 at 1e-13, exactly 0.0 at 3e-23 and 1e20) is REFUTED on current code. Control construction: over 4,000 random label multisets the pairing was a valid permutation 4000/4000 times, its label multiset equalled the true multiset 4000/4000 times, and its collision count equalled the arithmetic minimum max(0,2m-n) 4000/4000 times, with 0 index fixed points over 1,990 multisets with m<n -- so round-1 codex's RED (2/4 residual collisions on [A,A,B,B], 30/64 on 32A/32B) is REFUTED: I measure 0/4 and 0/64, 4/10 on 7A/3B and 6/10 on 8A/2B, each exactly the arithmetic minimum. Round-4 opus5's sole blocker -- that the Sattolo `_idx` was dead code -- is FIXED: `_shuf` is read at consistency.py:218. The hidden state is the right vector: hidden_states[-1] @ W_out^T reproduces each model's own logits with relative error 0.000e+00 on gpt2/distilgpt2/pythia-70m/pythia-160m, so the post-final-norm state is used. The untied-head branch is load-bearing and correct: on pythia-160m mean row-cos(W_out, W_in) is 0.000671 and using the input embedding table instead of lm_head.weight gives 0.000110 against the correct 0.031134 (282x). Identity mean(margin) == mean(raw) - mean(control) holds to 2.17e-19; an independent reimplementation of the estimator reproduces the headline to 1.14e-03 rel on gpt2 and 2.09e-04 rel on pythia-160m, both inside one control-resampling SD. 127/127 targeted tests and 11/11 scale-contract tests pass. What would have to change for GREEN: nothing -- it is already faithful. The residual token-id tie-break in the control is an arbitrary-but-valid choice within the defined class of controls, worth -1.72% on gpt2; it changes cross-model comparability, not what quantity is computed, and is scored on `comparable` and `defects` below.
comparable_reason: Comparable with a stated caveat. The quantity is dimension-free (a cosine), exactly invariant to isometries -- zero-padding moves the simplex margin by rel 0.00e+00 and an orthogonal map by 1.01e-07 -- and, thanks to the row-centring at consistency.py:101, exactly invariant to the softmax's additive row gauge W -> W + 1 v^T: on a REAL untied pythia-160m head at ||v||=84.40 (max softmax probability change 2.443e-04, i.e. float32 noise) the headline moves by rel 2.000e-07, while the UNCENTRED cosine collapses 0.948097359 -> 0.111954926 (-88.2%) under the same do-nothing transformation. Across 8 locally run models the headline is [gpt2 0.010260, distilgpt2 0.013715, gpt2-medium 0.015182, pythia-70m 0.021197, pythia-160m 0.031134, pythia-410m 0.089912, opt-125m 0.132287, SmolLM2-135M 0.058211] -- a 12.9x spread with Spearman rho(d_model) = +0.026 (p=0.95), so the spread is a model-FAMILY effect, not a size effect. Two residual caveats. (1) The metric is a cosine in the model's own final-layer frame, so it is not invariant to a function-preserving basis change: h -> hA, W -> W A^-T with A = diag(100,1,1) preserves the logits to max|dlogit| = 0.00e+00 yet moves the simplex margin 1.3333333 -> 0.0282807 (-97.88%), and A = diag(1,1,1e-3) gives -99.79%. That is inherent to the definition rather than a coding error, but it means cross-family comparisons carry a final-layer-conditioning component. (2) The control's equal-size group ordering tie-breaks by NUMERIC TOKEN ID (consistency.py:221, key `kv[0]`), so the shipped value sits below the ensemble of equally valid controls: over 200 randomized valid tie-breaks on gpt2 (14,875 positions) the ensemble is mean 0.010426981, sd 3.198e-05, range [0.010345733, 0.010528294], and the shipped 0.010248122 is z = -5.59, i.e. -1.72% and OUTSIDE the whole ensemble range; on pythia-160m the same test gives z = -0.77 / -0.46%. The effect is small in value and conservative in direction (BPE ids are frequency-ordered, so id-adjacent groups supply more similar control tokens, raising the control cosine and shrinking the margin), but it is a per-model arbitrary offset of up to 1.7% that no consumer can see.
github_reason: No code was ever released for this quantity because there is no source paper for it: task_metadata.py records it as `proxy-only` with provenance 'Output-projection geometry / logit-lens motivation (Belrose et al. 2023 tuned-lens as context)' and an EMPTY repo field. AlignmentResearch/tuned-lens implements a trained affine hidden->logit probe fitted by KL, a different object with no cosine and no derangement control, so it supplies no parity number; prior rounds confirmed 0 occurrences of `cosine` across its nn/lenses.py and nn/unembed.py. NONE is the accurate answer. In place of released code I verified against (a) analytic anchors -- the centred-simplex margin 4/3 matched to 5.96e-08 at every scale 1e-30..1e30, and the exact collision minimum max(0,2m-n) matched 4000/4000 times -- and (b) an INDEPENDENT reimplementation of the estimator written from the definition, which reproduces the shipped headline to 1.14e-03 rel on gpt2 (0.010248122 vs 0.010259816) and 2.09e-04 rel on pythia-160m (0.031127314 vs 0.031133806), both within one control-resampling SD.
paper_reason: There is no source paper and hence no published value to reproduce. Belrose et al. 2023 publish tuned-lens perplexities and KL curves, not a target-row cosine or a frequency-matched margin, and the BLME manuscript carries this task as a catalogue row with no defining equation. The reproducible anchors are therefore constructed rather than published, and the code matches all of them: the centred-simplex margin 4/3 = 1.3333333333 against a measured 1.3333332538604736 (rel 5.96e-08) at every scale from 1e-30 to 1e30; 0/4 residual collisions on [A,A,B,B] and 0/64 on 32A/32B; 4/10 on 7A/3B and 6/10 on 8A/2B, each the exact arithmetic minimum; and exactly 0.0 with _meta_control_collision_rate = 1.0 on an all-identical-token document, where every frequency-matched control is forced to equal the target and a zero margin is the correct answer.
confounds_reason: Not measurably a size or architecture proxy on the 8 models I ran locally (gpt2, distilgpt2, gpt2-medium, pythia-70m/160m/410m, opt-125m, SmolLM2-135M, spanning d_model 512-1024, 6-30 layers, vocab 49152-50304, 70M-405M params): Spearman rho(d_model) = +0.026 (p = 0.95), rho(n_layers) = +0.395 (p = 0.33), rho(vocab_size) = +0.350 (p = 0.40, Pearson -0.094), rho(params) = +0.548 (p = 0.16) -- none significant, and d_model is essentially zero. This REFUTES round-2/3/4 codex's r(vocab_size) = +0.843149/+0.843873, which was an n=4 artifact of a panel containing only two distinct vocabulary sizes; widening to n=8 collapses the vocabulary Pearson to -0.094. The quantity is dimension-free by construction (a cosine) and centring makes it exactly invariant to the softmax's additive row gauge (rel 2.0e-07 at ||v|| = 84.40 on a real untied head). The 12.9x cross-model spread is a model-FAMILY effect -- opt-125m 0.132287 against gpt2 0.010260 at the same d_model = 768 and vocab ~50k -- not a size effect.
defects: COMPARABILITY / CONTROL PROTOCOL (CODE: src/blme/tasks/geometry/consistency.py:220-222). The label groups are ordered by `sorted(_by_label.items(), key=lambda kv: (-len(kv[1]), kv[0]))`, so equal-size groups are tie-broken by NUMERIC TOKEN ID. The estimand admits any frequency-matched minimum-collision derangement, and the code computes a valid one exactly, but this particular one is biased: over 200 randomized valid tie-breaks on gpt2 (14,875 positions) the ensemble is mean 0.010426981, sd 3.198e-05, range [0.010345733, 0.010528294], and the shipped 0.010248122 is z = -5.59 / -1.72%, outside the entire range; on pythia-160m z = -0.77 / -0.46%. Mechanism: BPE ids are frequency-ordered, so id-adjacent groups donate more similar control tokens, inflating the control cosine and shrinking the margin. Direction is conservative (the margin is under-stated) and the size is <=1.7%, but it is an invisible per-model offset.

REPORTING: the normal-case output has 9 numeric keys and 0 uncertainty keys. The control is a SINGLE deterministic draw, so the consumer cannot separate the margin from control noise; the measured control-choice sd alone is 0.31% of the value on gpt2 and 0.60% on pythia-160m. Averaging the margin over R seeded valid controls and emitting a standard error would remove the 1.7% arbitrary component AND supply the missing uncertainty at negligible cost, since the per-token margins are already materialised.

DOC/STALE (consistency.py:44-47, 56-63, 105-111). Three docstring claims were measured BEFORE the unembedding rows were centred and are now false. (a) 'replacing every target with a uniformly random vocabulary row reproduces it to within 0.1-1.1% of its entire cross-model range' -- on current code _meta_prediction_alignment_uniform_baseline is 0.000158 against a raw mean of 0.021165 on gpt2 (0.75% of it, not ~100%), so the stated justification for demoting the raw cosine no longer holds. (b) 'gpt2's margin is NEGATIVE (-0.0077) and pythia-70m's is +0.00014' -- I measure prediction_alignment_margin_uniform = +0.021007 and +0.047800, a sign reversal on gpt2 and 341x on pythia-70m. (c) 'gpt2 reads +0.011443 within-document' -- current code reads +0.010260 on the same corpus construction.

CONFIG / PROTOCOL (src/blme/tasks/configs/defaults.yaml:104-105; src/blme/tasks/geometry/utils.py:460-461). The merged config is exactly {'num_samples': 100} while the manuscript specifies 200 hidden-state passages, and both collection routes hard-code max_length=512 against the manuscript's 128-token cap, with no way to change the window from defaults.yaml. This is a shipped-configuration divergence, not an implementation fault, and it does not qualify the GREEN verdict.

ARCHIVE INCOMPATIBILITY (already recorded in task_metadata.py, restated with current numbers): prediction_alignment_mean now holds the centred anisotropy-corrected margin (gpt2 0.010260) while archived runs hold the raw cosine (uncentred 0.948097 / centred raw 0.021165). Do NOT pool across the change.

PERFORMANCE, not correctness (consistency.py:187-190): the Sattolo pass makes one torch.randint call per position, roughly 14,900 CPU RNG calls per model at the shipped num_samples, inside a Python loop. One vectorised numpy Sattolo pass is identical in distribution and orders of magnitude cheaper.
fix: Nothing is required for implementation correctness. Recommended, in order of value: (1) drop the token-id tie-break -- order the label groups by their position in the already-computed Sattolo `_shuf` instead of by `kv[0]` at consistency.py:221 -- which removes the measured -1.72% / -5.59 SD gpt2 offset without touching the zero-collision guarantee, since the rotation argument depends only on the GROUP SIZES; (2) average the margin over R (say 20) seeded valid controls and emit `prediction_alignment_sem`, giving both a non-arbitrary control and the missing uncertainty; (3) re-measure and rewrite the three post-centring-stale docstring claims at lines 44-47, 56-63 and 105-111 (uniform baseline 0.000158 vs raw 0.021165 on gpt2; margin_uniform +0.021007 / +0.047800 for gpt2 / pythia-70m); (4) expose max_length in defaults.yaml and reconcile num_samples 100 vs the manuscript's 200; (5) add regression tests pinning the centred-simplex margin 1.3333333 at scales 1e-30 and 1e20, the 0/4 and 0/64 collision anchors, and the W -> W + 1 v^T gauge, none of which is currently asserted in an executable test.
